claims.text: High-temperature annealing induces structural relaxation in multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles.
High-temperature annealing annihilates defects in multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles.
Annealing-induced structural relaxation and defect annihilation preserve the nanoparticles' chemical stability under service conditions.
The initial nanoparticles are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid solutions with varying compositions and microstructures.
The controlled intervention is annealing at 1073 K for 12 hours with a heating rate of 5 K/min.
The annealing process will be observed in situ using TEM.
Thermal activation enables atomic rearrangement in the nanoparticles.
Thermally activated atomic rearrangement reduces defect density.
Defect reduction preserves the nanoparticles' near-equiatomic composition.
Preservation of near-equiatomic composition maintains chemical stability.
Annealed nanoparticles will have lower defect density than as-synthesized, unannealed nanoparticles.
Annealed nanoparticles will maintain their composition better than as-synthesized, unannealed nanoparticles under service regimes.
The hypothesized stability applies across 773–1173 K for catalytic operation.
The hypothesized stability applies across 473–1923 K for thermoelectric use.
